# Scrib SU -- 2026-08-25

Scheduled 10:00 to 10:30 CDT. The recording runs to 00:24:23, so the call came in
under the slot. Rob Forshier II, Pankaj Aggarwal, Nitish Goyal and Karuna
Arshakota all speak. Timestamps are offsets into
`knowledge/meetings/raw/2026-08-25-standup.vtt`.

## Summary

The last internal-only standup before the client joins from 2026-08-26 (Rob,
00:18:46). Nitish and Karuna dug into how the daily prompt works: for the MVP
it is one predefined prompt per day pulled from the database, the same prompt
for everyone in a region, with per-person uniqueness and region-based
variation left for later (Rob, 00:00:28 to 00:02:51; Karuna's region-testing
question, 00:03:02, answered as future scope). Rob called iOS first and Android second
(00:07:09). Pankaj then confirmed Expo as the framework in his ADR (00:08:39),
and raised a question not yet on the client board: can a web-app user join the same wall as mobile
users (00:08:03 to 00:09:56). Rob took that to the client the same afternoon.
Code starts in Bounteous repositories and moves to the client's repositories
later in the engagement; Pankaj flagged that this affects when CI/CD can
actually run through automated pipelines (00:05:35 to 00:06:04). Rob handed
Jira board ownership to the delivery team, asking them to write user stories
under the epics and features he had already prioritized from the POC
backlog, with the backlog fleshed out by end of week (00:10:58, 00:22:40).
Walking the app, Rob showed that walls are the channels of the product:
personal, family, and walls external to family (00:12:48, 00:18:22).

Nitish asked whether the client is weighing ways to charge for walls. Rob
said monetization is still undecided on the client side: possibly a limit on
how many walls a person can create, possibly a paid extra brush (Rob's
example figure was $1.99), or unlocking a color, such as orange, by play time
(00:17:06 to 00:17:53). None of this is decided, only under consideration,
and it feeds epic E17 in `tracking/backlog-epics.md`.

Rob also framed the calendar: this week and next are shape, focused on
access, devices, questions, and a flushed-out backlog, with real planning
starting once shape ends and heads-down delivery after that. He expects
additional funding to extend the engagement past the initial eight weeks
(00:23:25 to 00:24:02).

## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- One predefined daily prompt for the MVP, pulled from the database, owner: Rob Forshier II (00:02:51: "there'll just be some predefined single prompts per day, and that's it").
- Region-based validation testing is out of MVP scope, owner: Rob Forshier II (00:03:18, answering Karuna's 00:03:02 question).
- Expo stays the framework, owner: Pankaj Aggarwal (00:08:39, from his ADR; 00:09:10: "Expo is best now, so we should go with Expo now").
- Platform order is iOS first, Android second, owner: Rob Forshier II (00:07:09).
- Code starts in Bounteous repositories, moving to the client's repositories later in the engagement, owner: Rob Forshier II (00:05:35). Pankaj noted CI/CD timing depends on that move (00:05:46 to 00:06:04).
- Get the client's B2B source code, owner: Rob Forshier II. Rob raised it and committed to collecting it; Pankaj Aggarwal agreed it would help but did not propose it (00:06:34, 00:10:43).
- The delivery team owns the Jira board going forward, owner: Pankaj Aggarwal, Nitish Goyal, Karuna Arshakota (00:10:58). Rob handed over the epics and features he had prioritized from the POC backlog (00:04:52 to 00:05:11) and said unfit tickets can be discarded or repurposed and gaps added (00:22:40).
- Walls are the product's channels: personal, family, and walls external to family, owner: Rob Forshier II (00:18:22).
- Notifications are email plus in-app, owner: Rob Forshier II, confirming Nitish's question (00:16:35). Thinly evidenced. Nitish asked during Rob's demo and Rob answered "Right" over crosstalk, so confirm this one before relying on it.

### Questions

- Can a web-app user join the same wall as mobile users, and if so what compatibility layer is needed for sharing images and strokes between them? Raised by Pankaj Aggarwal, not yet on the client board (00:08:03 to 00:09:56). Rob's own read was that the client treats the web B2B app and the mobile B2C app as two separate products (00:10:16), and he took the question to the client that afternoon; per this repo's companion note (2026-08-25-scribl-shape-kickoff.md), the client confirmed the products stay separate, but that only answers the "two products" half, not whether a browser user could ever join a mobile wall.
- Is there a limit on how many walls a person can create? No limit today. Nitish Goyal asked (00:16:58); Rob said the client is still figuring out whether a wall-count limit is one of their monetization levers (00:17:06).
- How are walls ordered once a person creates more than the predefined set? Nitish Goyal asked (00:17:57); Rob said this needs a client conversation and is easy to implement once decided (00:18:22, 00:18:36).
- Can a person draw more than once a day? Karuna Arshakota asked (00:03:26). Rob described two existing POC mechanisms, challenges that generate extra prompts and prompt packs on a personal wall, but said the design still needs discussion (00:03:32 to 00:03:52). Not settled.
- Does an internal-only slot run before the client half of standup, and does the standup extend to an hour? Left open. Karuna and Pankaj leaned toward extending to an hour with the client joining the second half (00:19:29, 00:21:41, 00:22:08). Rob: "We don't have to make the decision now" (00:21:56).

- Rob Forshier II takes the web-app and wall-joining question to the client this same afternoon; blocked on the client's answer, which per the companion kickoff note came back the same day confirming two separate products, leaving the compatibility-layer half still open.

- The whole team runs the current one-slot standup format for a day or two before revisiting whether to extend it to an hour, per Pankaj Aggarwal's proposal; Karuna Arshakota and Rob Forshier II to reassess after that trial.
